analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md; the visible changed range is head lines 956-989, a new shape-warmup paragraph. The supplied units (head lines 1-415 and 416-797) are surrounding unchanged documentation, so they are orientation only. No code, key handling, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or protocol behavior is changed, and no threat-model control is weakened by the documentation change.

The described warmup is an excluded, bounded (20 s wall budget) set of synthetic probes that run once per loaded engine, using the artifact's default sampling. It trains no rate or counter. It is described as running after any passing self-test and before registration (or before a standalone listener opens), so routed consumer traffic should not interleave with it. The security-relevant questions are outside the supplied evidence. First, warmup probes could leave KV or prefix-cache state, so the code must not donate or persist them to the SSD prefix cache (T-041) or to the cross-tenant scope. Second, warmup must not emit cache receipts, usage records or billing events. Third, warmup must not bypass the slot's memory admission, because the 'solo prompt' and 'served width' cells allocate KV. The actual implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup) is not in the supplied batch, so these cannot be verified here. They are unverified contracts, not findings. The doc claims no probe trains rate or counters, and this is likewise unverified. A later pass should confirm that the warmup uses no cacheScope or cacheSalt, so it cannot donate to the SSD tier, and that it is excluded from telemetry and billing. Patch excerpt truncated at the end; remaining startup preload text was not seen.
